title.narrative: Emergency Food Security Support through Unconditional Cash Transfers and Agricultural Inputs for Drought-Affected Rural Communities in Afgoye district in Lower Shabelle region

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project will be implemented in Afgooye, targeting five highly vulnerable locations—Balgure, Sabiib, Canoole, Muuri, and Marerey. These villages were prioritized due to severe food insecurity, high vulnerability, and recurrent exposure to climate shocks, particularly drought and flooding.ltbrgtAn assessment conducted by AYUUB NGO from 20-25th November 2025 found critical food security conditions, with 88% of households consuming only one to two meals per day, 64% lacking stable income, and 55% relying on credit or food borrowing. Female-headed households and IDPs are disproportionately affected, with only 22% of pregnant and lactating women consuming protein-rich foods weekly. Harmful coping strategies are widespread, including reduced adult food intake (39%), withdrawal of children from school (25%), and early marriage as a survival strategy (13%). Damage to key infrastructure, including granaries for seed storage and a major irrigation canal, has further constrained access to food and water. Communities identified emergency cash combined with agricultural inputs (Cash Plus) as the preferred immediate and recovery response.ltbrgtAccording to IPC projections for October–December 2025, the population in the project area is classified under IPC Phase 3 (Crisis – 84,714 people) and IPC Phase 4 (Emergency – 11,427 people), reflecting significant food consumption gaps, rising market prices, limited income opportunities, and depletion of coping capacities. Riverine and ethnic minority communities face the highest risk of further deterioration.ltbrgtIn response, AYUUB NGO will deliver lifesaving emergency Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT) plus emergency agricultural inputs in (Cash+ approach) and Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT) to ensure vulnerable households’ immediate availability and access to food while also enabling them to produce locally and secure a harvest/food stock. The project will be in line with the SHF Reserve Allocation 2025 and Food Security Cluster strategy. The project will reach 1,400 households of 2988 Women, 1752 Girls, 1992 Men and 1668 boys. The total project budget is around 530,000 USD. 700 Vulnerable HHs will receive USD 55 per month for three months, aligned with the Minimum Expenditure Basket, with approximately 70% allocated to food and essential needs. Cash assistance will be complemented by emergency agricultural inputs, including maize, sorghum, cowpeas, vegetable and tools to support short-cycle food production and early livelihood recovery. The project will apply a Cash Plus approach, combining unconditional cash assistance with targeted livelihood support. Beneficiaries will be selected using vulnerability-based targeting. Evidence from AYUUB NGO 2025 pilot demonstrates that this approach improves equitable access, increasing minority clan inclusion from 30% to 40%. The intervention will prioritize underserved riverine villages predominantly inhabited by minority communities, which record critical GAM levels of 17.2% and face recurrent cyclical drought.ltbrgtProtection centrality, Accountability to Affected Populations, and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse are fully integrated in line with SHF/FSC strategic guideline. Protection-sensitive delivery, accessible and confidential feedback and complaints mechanisms, and PSEA reporting channels will be in place. All staff will adhere to a Code of Conduct and receive mandatory PSEA training, while communities will be informed of their rights and reporting options to ensure assistance is delivered safely, with dignity and accountability.ltbrgtGender and inclusion are central to the project design. Female-only Farmer Field Schools, flexible scheduling, and community-tailored input packages will address women’s time constraints. Nutrition messaging targeting vulnerable groups, particularly children and pregnant and lactating women, will be integrated into farmer training to improve dietary diversity and nutrition outcomes.ltbrgtlt/pgt
